iut_type: End Product (Allied Telesis GEN2 device), QDID combination disputed by another certification body
customer_question: Another certification body we consulted said the QDID combination you previously suggested for Bluetooth 5.1 is 'not certifiable,' citing a Consistency Check Error that would require the IC vendor (Silicon Labs) to change their ICS, and that Silicon Labs no longer supports older devices for such changes. Can you re-confirm whether this combination is actually certifiable?
question_variants: Is the other certification body's 'cannot certify' assessment correct?
Does a remaining Consistency Check Error always block new registration?
actual_issue: The customer received a conflicting assessment from a different certification body claiming the previously-recommended QDID combination could not be certified due to an unresolvable Consistency Check Error, creating uncertainty about whether to trust Allion's original recommendation or pursue an alternative path.
plain_english_explanation: Checking the specific QDID combination confirmed it does produce several genuine cross-layer inconsistencies (GAP/LL Mandatory-item conflicts) — so the other certification body's observation that an inconsistency exists was technically accurate. However, the conclusion that this inconsistency makes the combination entirely 'not certifiable' was not correct: since the registration references a QDID registered under an earlier certification rule set (PRD2.3), the specific request still satisfies particular conditions that allow new registration to proceed even with that inherited inconsistency present in the ICS. In other words, an inconsistency originating from an older, differently-ruled reference registration doesn't automatically disqualify a new registration from being possible — its registrability depends on the specific conditions involved, not simply on whether any inconsistency exists at all.
consultant_answer: We checked this combination and confirmed it does produce several genuine cross-layer inconsistencies (GAP/LL Mandatory-item conflicts), so the other certification body was right that an inconsistency exists. But their conclusion that this makes the combination entirely uncertifiable isn't correct: since this registration references a QDID registered under the earlier PRD2.3 rule set, your specific request still satisfies the particular conditions that allow new registration to proceed despite that inherited inconsistency. We can't share full details since you've consulted another body in parallel, but rest assured this combination remains certifiable.
decision_logic: The mere existence of a cross-layer Consistency Check inconsistency does not automatically disqualify a registration from proceeding — registrability depends on the specific conditions involved (such as whether the inconsistency originates from an older, differently-ruled reference registration), which requires checking the actual registration mechanics rather than applying a blanket 'any error means no certification' rule.
final_recommendation: When a customer relays a conflicting 'not certifiable' assessment from another certification body, independently re-verify the specific technical claim (does the inconsistency exist) separately from the broader conclusion (does it block certification), since the two don't necessarily follow from each other.
risk_if_done_wrong: Accepting another certification body's blanket 'not certifiable' conclusion without independently verifying the specific registrability conditions could cause the customer to abandon a viable, already-recommended registration path unnecessarily.
